answer.rationale: b1 confirms rollback cleared a checkout error spike without customer impact; b6 confirms staged gating/canary catches regressions within an hour — together they support a controlled re-deploy of a pre-patch build to a small cohort rather than a full reversion. Since compliance forbids reverting the security patch, I would NOT roll back the release outright. Instead I would: (1) freeze further rollout, (2) re-route or shade traffic away from the new build where safe, (3) if the write-path regression is in the patched code path, deploy the security fix as a hot-patch on the prior stable build. Given the constraint that only ONE intervention is allowed and the security patch must stay, the intended action is to halt the staged release and canary back to the prior stable build while carrying the security patch forward as a targeted hotfix — this is the only action that preserves both the compliance requirement and customer write availability.
